newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-S&P says raises Metway rating.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-S&P says raises Metway rating.

text.p: Standard and Poors Corp said on Thursday it has raised its long term counterparty rating on Metway Bank Ltd to A-minus from BBB-plus and removed it from creditwatch where it was placed on May 29.
S&P also said it had lowered the claims paying ability rating for Suncorp General Insurance Ltd and Suncorp Life and Superannuation Ltd to A-minus from AAA.
It has also lowered its counterparty rating on Queensland Industry Development Corp (QIDC) to A-minus/A2 from AAA/A1-plus.
S&P said Metway's rating outlook was stable.
It said the ratings actions were based on the benefits expected to be derived by the bank from its acquistion of the Suncorp group and QIDC.
Metway's A-2 short term counterparty rating has been affirmed.
"The downgrade of the Suncorp units and QIDC reflects the loss of the benefits of government ownership," S&P said.
The merger of the group will occur on December 1.
"Metway is expected to derive long-term benefits from its acquisition of the Suncorp group and QIDC," S&P said.

"Primarily the acquisition addresses some of the constraining factors that previously have impacted Metway's creditstanding and will assist to facilitate the transition of Metway into a stronger, more flexible and robust institution," the ratings agency said.
"The acquisition will enhance the diversity of Metway's business base and revenue generating streams," it said.
S&P noted residential mortgage loans of Queensland-based Metway would comprise 55 percent of total loans, which is less concentrated than other Australian regional banks.
It also noted that Metway would be the only Australian regional bank with a major presence in insurance.

"Through the acquisition, Metway will attain a strong market share in several core business lines in the regional market, including a pre-dominant position in retail deposits and general insurance," it said.
"The bank's profitability is expected to increase post-acquisition, and capitalisation will be adequate," it said.
